result.summary: Includes the network identifier in `CService::GetKey()` so that addresses on different networks (such as Tor and I2P) cannot produce identical key representations. Retains a legacy network-less key method specifically for `AddrMan` to preserve compatibility with existing `peers.dat` databases.
result.problem: Because `CService::GetKey()` omitted the network type, two addresses on different networks (such as Tor and I2P) could produce the same key bytes. In per-peer bloom filters tracking known addresses, this theoretical collision could cause a node to falsely believe a peer already knows an address (such as `foo.onion` after sending `foo.i2p`) and suppress relaying it.
evidence: PR description: "CService::GetKey() didn't include the network in the output. So in theory it would be possible for two IP2 and Tor addresses to have the same output... This would have unexpected results when used in the per-peer bloom filter of known addresses - we may wrongfully assume that a peer knows foo.onion when we have sent to them foo.i2p."
result.scope_notes: Diff was not available in metadata.
result.card: Adds the network type to `CService::GetKey()` to eliminate cross-network address key collisions between networks such as Tor and I2P. Without this, per-peer address bloom filters could falsely assume a peer already knows an address on one network because an address with matching key bytes was relayed on another, suppressing legitimate address announcements. A legacy key function without the network prefix is preserved for AddrMan to maintain backward compatibility with existing peers.dat files.
uncertainties: Diff was not provided to verify the implementation details of the new keying method and how AddrMan was isolated from the change.

risk.why: Mistakes in address key derivation or AddrMan key separation could disrupt address relay tracking or invalidate existing peers.dat files.
